This editor only edits the property animation flow that runs after a behavior is triggered. Configure events, triggers, and filters in the behavior panel.  Basics: drag nodes from the catalog onto the canvas; drag a node header to move it; drag from an output port to an input port to connect; use the × button on a connection to disconnect; drag empty canvas space with the left or right mouse button to pan; select a node and edit its properties on the right; right-click a node or press Delete to remove it.  Flow nodes: Start is the entry point and a graph should normally have one. End is the single ending point, and multiple branches can connect to End.In. Delay waits for a number of milliseconds. Sequence runs Step1, Step2, Step3 in order. Parallel runs Branch1, Branch2, Branch3 together and waits for all of them. If is an advanced text branch and is usually not needed for simple property animation.  Action nodes: Log writes preview text. SetProperty writes a property value, for example Target=Self, PropertyName=Opacity, Value=0.5. ResetProperty resets a property; PropertyName can be a specific property or All. AnimateProperty plays a property animation, for example Target=Self, PropertyName=Opacity, From=0, To=1, DurationMs=300, Easing=Linear. In preview, these actions are applied to the designer preview controls when a target scope is available.  Value nodes: Number/String/Boolean/Color store constant values for later value-port evaluation. ControlReference stores a target reference; Self is the common value today.

The node graph editor is a visual tool for composing control animations. Each graph consists of nodes and connections.
Nodes represent actions (e.g. set a property, play an animation); connections define execution order.
A graph starts at the Start node and ends at an End node.

Nodes fall into three categories: flow control nodes (control execution order), action nodes (manipulate control properties), and value nodes (provide constant data).

Drag nodes from the catalog on the left onto the canvas, or double-click a catalog item to quickly add it.
Drag from a node's output port (blue marker on the right) to another node's input port (marker on the left) to create a connection.
Click a node card to select it; the property panel on the right shows editable properties.
Press Delete to remove the selected node or connection. Use the toolbar buttons to duplicate a node or auto-create Start/End nodes.
Type keywords in the catalog search box to quickly find node types.

Flow Control Nodes:
Start — Entry point; each graph must have exactly one.
End — The single graph ending point; multiple branches can connect to the same End.In.
Delay — Waits for the specified number of milliseconds.
Sequence — Runs Step1 → Step2 → Step3 in order.
Parallel — Runs Branch1, Branch2, Branch3 simultaneously; continues when all complete.
If — Text comparison branch. Compares Left and Right, goes to True on match, False otherwise.

Action Nodes:
Log — Writes a line to the execution log for debugging.
SetProperty — Sets a control property value, e.g. Target=Self, PropertyName=Opacity, Value=0.5.
ResetProperty — Resets a control property. Use a specific property name or All.
AnimateProperty — Sends a property animation to the target control. Fill in PropertyName, From, To, DurationMs and Easing.

Value Nodes:
Number / String / Boolean / Color — Constant value nodes, editable in the property panel.
ControlReference — Target control reference; Self means the control this behavior is bound to.
When enabled, execution waits for the animation to finish before continuing.

Loop behaviors have three stage graphs: Start Graph, Loop Graph, and End Graph.

Preview one loop animation: runs Start Graph → runs Loop Graph once → runs End Graph.
Start loop animation preview: runs the Loop Graph repeatedly (controlled by RepeatCount and IntervalMs) until you click Stop loop animation preview.
Preview stop animation: runs only the End Graph so you can check the stop-stage effect.
Reset preview: restores all control properties modified by preview.

RepeatCount controls the number of loops; use a negative value for infinite looping until manually stopped. IntervalMs controls the wait time between loops; when it is 0, preview still keeps a short UI-friendly tick to avoid freezing the editor.

Preview does not run: check for a Start node, verify all nodes are connected, and look for validation errors.
Animation effect is unexpected: check AnimateProperty's From/To values and DurationMs, and verify the easing function.
Cannot connect nodes: make sure output port type (Flow/Value) matches input port type. Flow ports only connect to Flow ports; Value ports only connect to Value ports.
Graph execution hangs: check if a Delay node has an extremely large duration, or if all Parallel branches have End nodes.
Control animation has no effect: check that Target is correct (commonly Self) and PropertyName is spelled correctly (e.g. Opacity, Width, Height).
Delete: Delete selected node or connection
